note: Six distinct items, one trial each, temperature 0. Score = fraction of required fields correct across all six, with an item fully solved counting 1.0. Near-miss families per CARD_v2.md.

items.prompt: Emit ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: {"city": string, "temp_c": number}. The temperature is 7 degrees in Oslo. No prose, no code fences.
Emit ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: {"amount_cents": integer, "currency": string}. The invoice is 1250 cents in EUR. No prose, no code fences.
items.trap: Models reach for "amount" because it is the natural name. The schema says amount_cents.

items.prompt: Emit ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: {"priority": one of ["LOW","MEDIUM","HIGH"] (uppercase, exact), "id": integer}. Ticket id 88 is urgent. No prose, no code fences.
items.trap: Natural language says 'urgent'; the enum has no URGENT. The correct move is the nearest allowed value in the required casing.

items.prompt: Emit ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: {"count": integer, "ratio": number, "active": boolean}. There are 3 units, the ratio is one half, and it is active. No prose, no code fences.
items.trap: count must be the INTEGER 3, not "3"; ratio must be 0.5, not "1/2"; active must be a JSON boolean, not the string "true".

items.prompt: Emit ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: {"order_id": string, "shipping": {"postcode": string, "express": boolean}}. Order A-19 ships to postcode 101 with express delivery. No prose, no code fences.
items.trap: postcode is a STRING even though it looks numeric. Flattening the nested object loses the item.

items.prompt: Emit ONLY a JSON object {"readings": [ ... ]} where readings is an ARRAY of exactly 2 objects, each with keys {\"sensor\": string, \"value\": number}. The first is sensor A at 12. The second is sensor B at 12.5. No prose, no code fences.
items.trap: Exactly two elements, in order, each with both keys. Emitting one merged object, or three elements, loses the item.
